title: Fractera Data — the database of your node
description: The database every element of the node uses: each element its own tables in its own file, the deploy journal and the log of agent conversations, on your own computer.

blocks.pill: OpenSource Web4 agent & app starter kit
blocks.title: The database of your node
blocks.description: Every element keeps its tables here, each in its own database file opened by its own key. The deploy journal and the log of agent conversations live here too, on your own computer.

blocks.text: It reads and writes its tables through /db with its own key, which the installer put into its environment.
The element's tables sit in their own database file, data/elements/<id>.db, next to the node's file.
The core, the native elements and the main agent open any element's file with the node's data key.
Every deploy leaves a record, and the agents keep their conversations here, the last 10 000 of them.
Through the Cloudflare tunnel every door answers 404, with a key or without.

With the database element
rows: Every element would keep its data its own way
Every element keeps its tables behind one door
Two elements could write into one table by accident
Each element has its own database file, and a neighbour's table does not exist for it

It stays on your computer, inside your node

blocks.between: Each element opens the database with its own key, and a neighbour's table does not exist for it.

blocks.text: A call with an element's key works on that element's file. SQL that reaches for another file, such as ATTACH, is refused.

The node's data key works on the node's own file, and on any element's file when the call names it with ?space=<element>. Tables an element wrote into the node's file before it had its own are copied over by the architect's word (/db/claim).
The database keeps the doors apart, not the disk: every file lies in this element's folder on your computer, and all elements run as one user of it.
Every element of the node already has the database address and its own key. Read ten rows of a table:

A table is declared by the element that owns it, once, at its start: CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS through POST /db/migrate. A call returns at most 1000 rows, and columns such as password never leave the database.

head: Part
What it does
rows: SQLite
One file for each element and one for the node, in this element's folder, never in git
/db/tables
Rows: read with search, limit and offset, insert one, edit one by its id
/db/migrate
The schema and any SQL, with a key only, never from a browser session
/deploy-runs
The deploy journal of every element of the node
/a2a-log
The agents' conversations, the last 10 000, fields named like secrets stripped
/media, /vectors
Passed on to the storage and vectors elements, the answers unchanged
